messages:
Sam: Heads-up—prototype for a 'price horizon + SLA weighting' spot bid policy. Trying to avoid churny oscillations where we flip to cheap pools then instantly get evicted. TL;DR: pay a little more when SLA impact is high and prefer capacity-optimized across shorter horizons.
Maria: can you sketch the knobs? curious how it ties to warmbuffer and preemptible spillbacks.
Sam: sure. basic idea: rather than a single price floor, we compute a dynamic bid budget over a time horizon (e.g., 20–60m) and weight bids by request SLA tier. So high-SLA traffic gets a multiplier. Also prefer capacity-optimized pools for horizons < 30m.
Kai: this seems reasonable. How do we measure SLA impact per job? per-customer? per-route?
Sam: per-route for now. Each route has an SLA score (0..1) derived from p95 latency importance + business weight. Multiply bid_budget = base_budget * (1 + sla_score * sla_weight).
Jen: example values? makes it easier to evaluate.
Sam: example config (prototype):
```
bid_policy:
  horizon_minutes: 30
  sla_weight: 0.7  # 0 = price-only, 1 = SLA dominates
  price_delta_pct: 12  # willing to pay x% above price-optimal to tilt to capacity-opt
  prefer_capacity_opt_for_short_horizons: true
  short_horizon_threshold_min: 25
  warmbuffer_target_minutes: 10
```
Maria: good. what about multi-region behavior? if one region is evictiony we should shift across regions even if network egress costs rise.
Sam: yes — add a regional risk factor based on recent eviction rate & spot scarcity. It reduces effective bid budget in riskier regions, unless SLA weight forces us. Also add hysteresis to avoid flip-flops (cooldown window).
Kai: eviction signal source? cloud spot events + our node-drain events + marketplace price spikes?
Sam: all of the above. ops-bot streams spot-event webhooks into infra metrics; we aggregate into a per-region rolling eviction_rate.
ops-bot: deployed new eviction-rate metric stream to prometheus job: ec2_spot_evictions_total by region (interval=60s).
Jen: rollout plan? I'd prefer a canary: route few high-sla customer requests into the new policy, measure p99 and price delta.
Maria: agree. add a fallback rule: if eviction_rate > 0.03 and losses > 10% over 15m, revert route to reserved/dedicated or warmbuffer.
Sam: canary plan sketch:
- Canary window: 2h for 3 routes (low, medium, high SLA)
- Metric hooks: p95 latency, eviction_count, dollars/hr, failed-starts
- Auto rollback: if p95 increase > 20% or eviction delta > 0.02 in 15m
- Observability: tag traces with bid_policy=horizon-sla

Kai: curious about cost math. if sla_weight=0.7 and price_delta_pct=12 we might pay 10–15% more but reduce evictions by 30–50% for short seq workloads. worth it for interactive use.
Jen: also check GPU SKU mix: cheaper SKUs often have higher eviction variance. we should make sku_score part of capacity preference.
Sam: yes — maintain sku_score = historical_eviction_rate * eviction_penalty + perf_score. Then capacity_opt_score = f(region_score, sku_score).
Maria: any quick experiments to run this week? we could run an A/B across two small clusters with identical traffic patterns.
Sam: plan: spawn two 100-GPU pools in us-west-2: pool-A price-optimized, pool-B horizon-sla. Replay synthetic traffic with mixed seq lengths + p95 webhook. Run for 6h overnight and compare cost/evictions/latency.
Jen: I'll add the experiment to the infra-experiments board and grab the budgets.
Kai: one more safety ask: ensure nodes with active KV cache get higher preemption grace (soft-evict), or we prioritize draining nodes with cold caches. Otherwise model startup cost spikes.
Sam: noted — drain-priority will include cache_warmth. good call.
Maria: awesome. if experiment looks good we can prototype a gradual rollout tied to route weights and warmbuffer sizing.
Sam: thanks everyone. I'll push the prototype branch and attach the experiment playbook. cc @Maria for canary coord.
ops-bot: created experiment ticket INFEXP-2917 and scheduled infra job for 03:00 UTC.
